name: MrOS lateral spine radiographs (Osteoporotic Fractures in Men)
what: lateral thoracic and lumbar films of 5,994 men at six US centres, two visits (2000-2002 and about 4.6 years later), with Genant semi-quantitative vertebral fracture grades per vertebra; one deep-learning study used 4,461 subjects and 15,524 films; the image counts and the request steps to confirm on the page
level_truth: Genant grades on named levels, so level truth exists
licence: a MrOS data request agreement; terms to confirm on the page
how_to_get: Request the lateral spine films through the NIA Aging Research Biobank (https://agingresearchbiobank.nia.nih.gov): log in or create an account there, open Requests, Request for Materials, choose Images at the top of the form and name the MrOS study; the biobank's sample agreement and costs pages give the terms and fees, and the request, the agreement and any fee are the owner's hand; the proposal text is letters/mros_lateral_spine.md.
MrOS Online itself (https://mrosonline.ucsf.edu/) is closed to registrations until its NIH update is done; the centre writes when it reopens, and the reading tables may still come from there.
Once granted, fetch by the route the centre gives, as a Slurm job on the owner's word, never on the login node; no fetch helper applies until the route is known.
source_status: found by the sweep of 2026-10-21; not fetched; a research data request through the MrOS coordinating centre (an online application with a proposal), not sent; the images are not on dbGaP, whose phs000373 covers genotypes (to confirm on the page); older osteoporotic spines with compression fractures, the anatomy the C-arm sees in kyphoplasty
result: Asked 2026-10-22 by the owner: an email to MrOSData@ucsf.edu for authorization to register on MrOS Online. the MrOS coordinating centre (Liezl Concepcion, Center for Aging Science, Sutter Health Research Institute) replied 2026-10-22 18:16 UTC: the portal is closed to registrations while it is updated for new NIH requirements, they will write when it reopens; the study images are being added to the NIA's Aging Research Biobank (https://agingresearchbiobank.nia.nih.gov), where the request should go. Since the biobank already has the images, it can give the timeline, the transfer, any fees and the terms.
